body.statement: For every member of \(\mathfrak M\) there is a common \(G_{\infty}\in C^3(\mathcal K;\mathbb S_{+}^{Fp})\) such that, for every balanced \(m=m(n)\) with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), \[\max_{0\le j\le3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\lVert D_{\rho}^{j}G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}G_{\infty}(\beta)\rVert\to0,\] and \[\max_{0\le j\le3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\lVert D_{\rho}^{j}G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}G_{\infty}(\beta)\rVert\xrightarrow{P_{S_m}}0.\] Here \(D_{\rho}^{0}G=G\), the first display is deterministic conditional on the complete baseline array, and the second probability is over the uniform pilot split conditional on that array.
body.justification: The common experiment-indexed limit removes ambiguity about which empirical oracle and which convergence mode define the boundary constants.
body.gap: First-order learned-rerandomization arguments require consistency of one selected score, whereas the second-order boundary expansion needs uniform convergence of the oracle map and its first three quotient derivatives along both realized experiment sequences.
body.consumer: It gives replication planners one stable limiting geometry whether the oracle is evaluated on all registered units or on the random main-wave complement.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\mu_{q,\beta}(x)=E_{\beta}\{Y(q)\mid X=x\}\) and \(v_{q,\beta}(x)=E_{\beta}\{Y(q)^2\mid X=x\}\).  For \(0\leq j\leq3\), let \(\mathscr F_j\) be the finite collection consisting of all scalar coordinates of the functions needed to form the assignment covariance \(\operatorname{Cov}_{\beta}\{\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(0),\Delta_T\}\) and the imbalance covariance \(\operatorname{Var}(\Delta_T)\), after applying \(D_{\rho}^{j}\).  Direct expansion of the two finite sums defining \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(0)\) and \(\Delta_T\) shows that these functions are finite products and linear combinations of coordinates of \(x\), \(xx^{\mathsf T}\), \(D_{\rho}^{\ell}\mu_{q,\beta}(x)\), and \(D_{\rho}^{\ell}v_{q,\beta}(x)\), where \(q\in\mathcal Q\) and \(0\leq\ell\leq j\).  The exact coefficients are the balanced-assignment probabilities
\[
 P(Z_i=q)=\frac1Q,
 \qquad
 P(Z_i=q,Z_j=q)=\frac{k-Q}{Q^2(k-1)},
 \qquad
 P(Z_i=q,Z_j=q')=\frac{k}{Q^2(k-1)}quad(q\ne q',\ i\ne j).
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus no distributional approximation is used in this reduction.

By \(\mathrm{ass{:}arraywise\text{-}moment\text{-}regularity}\), every member of every \(\mathscr F_j\) is jointly continuous and uniformly bounded on the common compact set \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal K\).  Joint continuity on a compact set gives uniform equicontinuity in \(\beta\).  If \(\nu_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{x_{in}}\), then \(\mathrm{ass{:}baseline\text{-}limit}\) gives, for every fixed \(\beta\), convergence of the integral of each such function under \(\nu_n\) to its integral under \(\nu\).  A finite \(\beta\)-net and uniform equicontinuity therefore yield
\[
 \max_{0\leq j\leq3}\ \max_{f\in\mathscr F_j}
 \sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
 \left|\int f(x,\beta)\,\nu_n(dx)-\int f(x,\beta)\,\nu(dx)\right|\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{2}
\]
This is the standard finite-net proof: for a net point use weak convergence, and for an arbitrary \(\beta\) bound the two off-net differences by the common modulus of continuity.

For any split \(S\) of size \(m\), put \(T=S^c\), so \(|T|=N\).  For a function bounded in absolute value by \(C\), the identity
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{i\in T}f(x_{in},\beta)-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nf(x_{in},\beta)
 =\frac mN\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nf(x_{in},\beta)-\frac1m\sum_{i\in S}f(x_{in},\beta)\right\}
\]
implies
\[
 \sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
 \left|\frac1N\sum_{i\in T}f(x_{in},\beta)-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nf(x_{in},\beta)\right|
 \leq \frac{2Cm}{N}=o(1).
 \tag{3}
\]
The same bound applies to all members of all \(\mathscr F_j\).  Hence (2)--(3) give a common limit, uniformly through three \(\rho\)-derivatives, for every empirical moment entering the full-array and complement oracle constructions.  The complement convergence is in fact uniform over all splits, and therefore implies the asserted convergence in \(P_{S_m}\)-probability.

We next propagate these moment limits through the two matrix operations in \(\mathcal B_T\).  Let \(S_T=|T|^{-1}\sum_{i\in T}(x_{in}-\bar x_T)(x_{in}-\bar x_T)^{\mathsf T}\).  Expanding \(\Delta_T\) and using (1) and the Walsh identities \(\sum_qc_q=0\) and \(\mathbf C^{\mathsf T}\mathbf C=QI_F\), one obtains
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\Delta_T)=\frac4{k-1}\,(I_F\otimes S_T).
 \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, \(\Delta_T=(2/k)\sum_{i\in T}c_{Z_i}\otimes(x_{in}-\bar x_T)\), while \(E(c_{Z_i}c_{Z_i}^{\mathsf T})=I_F\) and \(E(c_{Z_i}c_{Z_j}^{\mathsf T})=-I_F/(k-1)\) for \(i\ne j\).  The same expansion (1) shows that \((k-1)\operatorname{Cov}_{\beta}\{\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(0),\Delta_T\}/4\) is a finite linear combination of the empirical moments already controlled in (2)--(3).  Multiplying both covariance factors in the definition of \(\mathcal B_T\) by \((k-1)/4\) does not change their product.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}baseline\text{-}gram}\), the eigenvalues of \(S_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}\) are bounded away from zero and infinity.  Equation (3), applied to the first two baseline moments, gives the same bounds for every complement once \(m/n\to0\).  Consequently the Moore--Penrose inverse in \(\mathcal B_T\), after this common scaling, is an ordinary inverse on the relevant range, and inversion is uniformly smooth there.  Differentiating the identity \(AA^{-1}=I\),
\[
 D(A^{-1})[H]=-A^{-1}HA^{-1},
 \tag{5}
\]
and iterating (5) through order three proves that the covariance limit from (2)--(3) propagates uniformly through \(\operatorname{Var}(\Delta_T)^{+}\).  It follows that there is a \(C^3\) matrix map \(\mathcal B_{\infty}(\beta)\) satisfying
\[
 \max_{0\leq j\leq3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
 \left\|D_{\rho}^{j}\mathcal B_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}\mathcal B_{\infty}(\beta)\right\|\to0
 \tag{6}
\]
and the identical conclusion for \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\), uniformly over the split.

Set \(M_T(\beta)=\mathcal B_T(\beta)^{\mathsf T}W\mathcal B_T(\beta)\) and \(M_{\infty}(\beta)=\mathcal B_{\infty}(\beta)^{\mathsf T}W\mathcal B_{\infty}(\beta)\).  Since \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^{F}\), these matrices are positive semidefinite, and (6) plus the product rule gives
\[
 \max_{0\leq j\leq3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
 \left\|D_{\rho}^{j}M_T(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}M_{\infty}(\beta)\right\|\to0
 \tag{7}
\]
along both experiment-indexed sequences.  On the constant positive-rank stratum imposed by \(\mathrm{ass{:}oracle\text{-}rank}\), \(M_{\infty}(\beta)\ne0\).  Continuity and compactness therefore give
\[
 \inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{tr}M_{\infty}(\beta)>0.
 \tag{8}
\]
By (7)--(8), the trace denominator is also uniformly positive for the two finite-array sequences for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The quotient rule through order three now applies uniformly to
\[
 G_T(\beta)=\mathcal N\{M_T(\beta)\}
 =\frac{M_T(\beta)}{\operatorname{tr}M_T(\beta)}.
\]
Defining
\[
 G_{\infty}(\beta)=\frac{M_{\infty}(\beta)}{\operatorname{tr}M_{\infty}(\beta)}
\]
therefore proves both displayed convergences in the lemma, including all \(\rho\)-derivatives of orders zero through three.  Positivity, trace one, (8), and the quotient rule also show \(G_{\infty}\in C^3(\mathcal K;\mathbb S_+^{Fp})\), completing the proof.
